reproduction_target: Two computational scopes inside a wet-lab-anchored method-comparison study of Metagenomic Sequencing with Spiked Primer Enrichment (MSSPE) vs untargeted mNGS on swine slurry / farm wastewater. (i) Primer design: the authors' own open-source Rust pipeline 'Open MSSPE Design' (MAFFT alignment + segmentation, 15-nt k-mer enumeration, greedy set-cover selection, Primer3/ntthal thermodynamic filtering, cross-dimer graph pruning) producing 15 virus-specific spiked-primer panels. (ii) Downstream analysis: CZ ID cloud metagenomic classification of the sequenced libraries against NCBI NT/NR, Geneious Prime read mapping for genome-coverage statistics, and an R analysis stack (rPM enrichment ratios, Wilcoxon signed-rank + Benjamini-Hochberg, McNemar odds ratios, rarefaction/downsampling with observed-richness alpha diversity, binomial GLMM for detection probability, and figure/table rendering). Physical sampling, PEG concentration, nucleic-acid extraction, oligo synthesis, library preparation and Illumina sequencing are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, derived from the bioRxiv JATS XML Methods prose (fetched by curl to /tmp/stage1_10.64898_2025.12.26.690930/paper.xml; WebFetch on the same URL returned HTTP 403). Title-phrase grep confirmed the correct paper ('Targeted metagenomic sequencing with spiked primers...', 4 hits). Both cited code repositories resolve 200 and their README prose was read at landing-page level only; no workflow source was read line-by-line (Stage 2 work). Statistical procedures inside the R stack were grouped into four steps (coverage+enrichment statistics, rarefaction, GLMM, figure/table rendering) rather than one step per test, because the Methods name one R environment and one repository rather than separate tool invocations. 7 wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Multiple-sequence alignment of full-length viral genomes retrieved from NCBI GenBank using MAFFT v7.388 (algorithm=Auto, 200 PAM/k=2, gap open 1.53, offset 0.123), then partitioning into overlapping segments (default 500 nt window, 250 nt overlap) — invoked inside Open MSSPE Design

Spiked-primer panel design with Open MSSPE Design (stated v1.0; Rust; kmer-size=15, min-tm=30, max-tm=60, otherwise defaults): k-mer enumeration from segment termini, greedy set-cover selection (default 1000 iterations), Primer3 nearest-neighbour Tm/dG characterisation, filtering at +/-2 SD Tm and dG < -9 kcal/mol, all-vs-all ntthal cross-dimer graph pruning
In-silico validation of designed spiked-primer sequences for binding efficiency / target-consensus amplification using Geneious Prime v2025.1.3 (proprietary GUI software)

CZ ID (czid.org) cloud metagenomic pipeline: quality filtering, human-read removal, random subsampling to 2 million unique reads, assembly, and read/contig taxonomic assignment against NCBI NT and NR; mass-normalised ERCC background model with thresholds z-score > 1, mean alignment length > 50 bp, and >= 1 rPM / 3 reads / 1 contig — no pipeline version and no NT/NR database snapshot date stated

Genome-coverage statistics in Geneious Prime v2025.1.3: CZ ID-exported unique reads mapped with the default Geneious mapper at highest sensitivity, MSSPE reads trimmed 15 nt at 5' and 3' ends, mapped to eight named reference accessions (KY489985, OL677619, MZ328119, M20325, NC_027054, NC_023675, ON375367, OL944705)

Coverage-fraction computation and enrichment statistics in R v4.5.0 (analysis repo github.com/mattparkerls/metagenomic-spiked-primer-enrichment-paper): ERCC-normalised rPM, MSSPE/mNGS fold-change with pseudocount rPM=0.1, Wilcoxon signed-rank with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, rank-biserial effect size, McNemar test and pooled odds ratios

Rarefaction / depth downsampling in R: taxon-level read counts randomly subsampled without replacement to target depths (100,000-1.5 million reads), 15 independent rarefaction replicates per sample per library-prep method, observed-richness alpha diversity, Friedman rank test, detection thresholds of 5/10/15 reads — no RNG seed stated in prose

Binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model of detection probability (LibraryPrep + DepthScaled + interaction, random intercepts for viral target and sample) fitted in R with lme4/glmmTMB; Pearson-residual overdispersion check and Nakagawa marginal/conditional R-squared

Figure and table rendering from five R Markdown documents (primer_tables, msspe_enrichment, sequencing_performance, sequencing_depth, microbial_community) knitted to PDF via XeLaTeX, using ggplot2, tidyverse, vegan, phyloseq, patchwork, kableExtra, purrr, ggpubr, stringr, performance, viridis, superheat — no package versions pinned anywhere
Grab sampling of 25 wastewater and swine slurry samples from smallholder farms in northern Thailand
PEG precipitation concentration and bead-bashing homogenisation of solid-rich samples
Proteinase K treatment and parallel DNA/RNA extraction with on-column DNase I (Zymo Quick DNA/RNA Microprep Plus, Zymo Pathogen Magbead), Qubit/Nanodrop QC
Spiked-primer oligonucleotide synthesis and pooling (IDT oPools, 10 nmol scale, 6 nmol per oligo, resuspended in IDTE pH 8.0)
Internal process control preparation (ZymoBIOMICS Fecal Reference D6323 and wastewater RNA spiked with HeLa cell RNA)
Paired library preparation (NEBNext Ultra II, ERCC Spike-In Mix 25 pg/uL, FastSelect rRNA depletion, random hexamers; MSSPE arm additionally spiked with primers at 1:2 volume ratio)
Two-step normalisation pooling and Illumina sequencing (iSeq 100 pilot, then NextSeq 2000 or NovaSeq X 1.5B, 150 bp paired-end)

headline.static_readiness: 0/9 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 6/9 computational steps (C1, C2, C6, C7, C8, C9). The remaining 3/9 cap at NI: C3 and C5 depend on proprietary Geneious Prime v2025.1.3 GUI work (code axis 0, proprietary ceiling), and C4 runs on the hosted CZ ID platform with no pipeline version and no NCBI NT/NR snapshot date (version axis 0). This paper is unusually well-provisioned for a mixed wet-lab study - two live MIT-licensed repositories, an SRA BioProject, a public protocol document, and exact pins on MAFFT v7.388, Geneious v2025.1.3 and R v4.5.0 - but no step can exceed RI at Stage 1 or Stage 2 without an environment capture that provides closure, and none is claimed: the R analysis repo has no renv.lock, no Dockerfile, no conda spec and no package version pins (README states only 'R >= 4.1'), and the Rust repo pins the Rust toolchain only as 'latest stable' with mafft and primer3 installed via unpinned brew.
headline.coverage: 9 computational steps assessed from bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods prose plus the landing pages/READMEs of the two cited GitHub repositories. 7 wet-lab steps (sampling, PEG concentration, extraction, oligo synthesis, process controls, library prep, sequencing) counted in W and verdicted X as out-of-scope. Computational coverage = 9/16 = 56%.

gaps.where: Whole analysis environment, both repositories (C1, C2, C6, C7, C8, C9)
gaps.missing: No environment capture with closure is claimed anywhere. The R analysis repo README states only 'R >= 4.1 with XeLaTeX installed (TinyTeX or TeX Live)' and lists 14 packages with no versions; there is no renv.lock (raw.githubusercontent .../main/renv.lock -> 404), no Dockerfile, no conda/pixi spec. The Rust repo README specifies 'Rust (latest stable version)' with no toolchain pin and installs mafft and primer3 via 'brew install' with no version. A Cargo.lock is present in the Rust repo tree (od-msspe/Cargo.lock -> HTTP 200) but it is auto-generated, is not claimed as an environment capture in paper or README, and pins only crate dependencies - not the Rust toolchain, not mafft, not primer3, not the platform. Under the Step-8 symmetric env-closure gate this fails closure, so every step stays at version=1.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a renv.lock (or conda-lock/pixi.lock) pinning R 4.5.0 plus all analysis package versions and their CRAN/Bioconductor snapshot, and a container digest or rust-toolchain.toml + pinned mafft/primer3 versions for the primer-design pipeline.

gaps.missing: The Methods name the CZ ID platform and cite the CZ ID paper, but state no pipeline/workflow version and no date of analysis. CZ ID workflow versions change the QC, assembly and alignment behaviour, so the executed pipeline state is not identifiable from the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the CZ ID workflow version (and project/sample IDs or a shared CZ ID project link) used for each sequencing run.

gaps.where: CZ ID taxonomic assignment against NCBI NT and NR (C4)
gaps.missing: The reference databases are given only as 'NCBI's nucleotide (NT) and non-redundant (NR) protein databases' with no index build date, version or accession snapshot. NT/NR are rolling resources; taxonomic calls, rPM values and the enrichment and detection statistics that derive from them are not re-derivable from the stated information. Stage-1 prose cannot assign env_capture_class (that is Stage-2, from workflow code), but the prose alone pins nothing.
gaps.how_to_close: State the NT/NR index date used by the CZ ID run (CZ ID reports this per-sample), or export and deposit the taxon-count tables that the downstream R analysis actually consumes.

gaps.where: Geneious Prime v2025.1.3 in-silico primer validation and read mapping (C3, C5)
gaps.missing: Two analysis steps run in commercial closed-source GUI software. The version is pinned and the mapper setting ('default Geneious mapper', 'highest sensitivity') and trimming (15 nt at each end) are described, but the code is not inspectable and a licence is required, so these steps carry the proprietary ceiling of NI. The mapping output that feeds the R coverage calculation is not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Re-run or cross-check the mapping with an open aligner (e.g. bowtie2/minimap2) with recorded parameters, or deposit the per-target BAM/coverage tables exported from Geneious so the downstream R computation is independently checkable.

gaps.missing: The README documents 'data/: Input data and per-experiment folders (experiment_1/, experiment_2/, experiment_3/, experiment_all/)' but /data/ is listed in .gitignore and is absent from the published tree (verified against the GitHub trees API: only .gitignore, LICENSE, README.md, helper_utils.R, five analysis folders with their .Rmd files, and pre-rendered figures/tables). The .Rmd scripts are therefore not runnable as shipped - the immediate inputs (CZ ID export tables, metadata, primer tables) are not published, and the Data-availability statement points only to raw reads in SRA plus 'available from co-corresponding authors'.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the data/ directory (or a Zenodo archive of it) containing the CZ ID export CSVs and sample metadata that the .Rmd files read, and remove /data/ from .gitignore or document the archive location in the README.

gaps.missing: The Methods state 'We used Open MSSPE Design (v1.0)'. The repository's published releases and tags are v1.2.0, v1.1.0 and 'before-lint-fix' (GitHub releases/tags API, checked 2026-07-28); no v1.0 release or tag exists. The stated pin therefore does not resolve to a retrievable code state, so the code axis is 'reconstructable' rather than 'public+exact'.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the exact commit SHA or an existing release tag (or create/restore the v1.0 tag), and ideally archive the used state to Zenodo with a versioned DOI.

gaps.missing: 'full-length viral genomes were retrieved from NCBI GenBank' for fifteen primer sets, with no accession list, no download date, no per-virus genome counts and no deposited input FASTA. The alignment that the greedy set-cover operates on cannot be reconstructed, so the designed primer panels are not re-derivable even with the pipeline in hand. The output primer sequences are provided (Supplementary Data 1), but not the inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the input FASTA files (or the per-virus GenBank accession lists plus retrieval date) alongside the primer panels.

gaps.where: Rarefaction / downsampling and CZ ID 2-million-read subsampling (C7, C4)
gaps.missing: Two stochastic steps with no RNG seed reported in prose: CZ ID 'randomly subsamples unique QC- and human-filtered reads to 2 million reads', and the R analysis performs 'random subsampling without replacement' with 15 independent rarefaction replicates per sample per depth. Without a seed the rarefaction curves and detection proportions are reproducible only distributionally.
gaps.how_to_close: Set and report an RNG seed in the .Rmd chunks (and check whether it is actually consumed by the subsampling helper in helper_utils.R - a Stage-2 check), and state the CZ ID subsampling seed if the platform exposes it.

gaps.where: R package versions across the analysis stack (C6, C7, C8, C9)
gaps.missing: R is pinned to v4.5.0 in the Methods but the README asks only for 'R >= 4.1', and none of the 14+ packages (tidyverse, ggplot2, vegan, phyloseq, lme4, glmmTMB, patchwork, kableExtra, emmeans, taxize, magick, pdftools, superheat, performance, viridis, purrr, ggpubr, stringr) carries a version. lme4/glmmTMB optimiser defaults and vegan/phyloseq diversity implementations change across releases, which bears directly on the GLMM and alpha-diversity results. Note also a prose/README discrepancy: the Methods list 'phyoseq' (phyloseq) and do not name glmmTMB or emmeans, while the README names glmmTMB, emmeans and taxize and omits phyloseq - so the two version lists disagree about which packages were used.
gaps.how_to_close: Record sessionInfo() output in each rendered document and pin the package set with renv.

gaps.missing: Sampling, PEG concentration, extraction, oligo synthesis, process-control preparation, paired library preparation and Illumina sequencing are physical sequence-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (7) and verdicted X, excluded from the |S|=9 denominator.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. The reproducible entry point is the raw read set in SRA BioProject PRJNA1391017; a public protocols document (Google Docs) covers the bench procedure.
